svg.title: KFold, GroupKFold, and TimeSeriesSplit folds compared
svg.desc: Three cross-validation splitters drawn as grids, one row per fold and one cell per row of data. KFold or StratifiedKFold shuffles rows into five folds, so each fold's test cells are scattered; that is fine when rows are independent, and stratified folds keep the 3 percent spam rate in every fold. GroupKFold labels cells by workspace, A to J with two sessions each, and every fold holds out whole workspaces, so no workspace appears in both training and test; on the same 12,000 sessions, shuffled KFold reports ROC-AUC 0.958 while GroupKFold reports 0.725. TimeSeriesSplit orders cells by time: each fold trains on all earlier cells and tests on the next block, later cells stay unused, and the training window grows from fold 1 to fold 4; use it for forecasts and anything that drifts.

g.text: Three ways to cut data into cross-validation folds
KFold or StratifiedKFold: rows shuffled into 5 folds
GroupKFold: all sessions of a workspace stay in one fold
TimeSeriesSplit: train on the past, test on the next block
time: oldest rows on the left
Choose the splitter that copies how new data arrives: by row, by entity, or by time.
